constraint_classes.UNVERIFIED_HYPOTHESIS: proposed as an explanation; requires investigation
constraint_classes.POTENTIAL_BOTTLENECK: a plausible limiting condition exists; its effect is not established
constraint_classes.VERIFIED_RESTRICTION: a rule or limit demonstrably applies to this activity. It says what MAY NOT happen. It does not say that this is what currently limits output -- another condition may bind first.
constraint_classes.CONSTRAINT_UNDER_SCENARIO: becomes limiting when stated assumptions hold; the scenario must be named
constraint_classes.OBSERVED_CONSTRAINT: evidence establishes that this condition limits this activity -- typically an actor observed acting on it
constraint_classes.BINDING_ECONOMIC_CONSTRAINT: evidence establishes that this condition CURRENTLY determines the activity's feasible output. Requires that the competing candidates have been addressed, because only one thing binds at a time and naming it means ruling the others out.

constraint_rule: BINDING and OBSERVED both require an OBSERVED LINK between the condition and the activity. Co-presence in a region is not a link.

demonstrations.question: Under what conditions could an investment in water or wastewater infrastructure make additional housing development feasible?

constraints.condition: New Mexico is in drought (79.25% of area in D2 or worse)
constraints.activity: the 380-unit Los Alamos workforce housing project
constraints.means: a plausible limiting condition exists; its effect is not established
constraints.why: the attempt that must fail. Both facts are real and the inference between them is not evidence.
constraints.refused: K_DROUGHT_HOUSING: BINDING_ECONOMIC_CONSTRAINT requires an OBSERVED LINK between 'New Mexico is in drought (79.25% of area in D2 or worse)' and 'the 380-unit Los Alamos workforce housing project'. Both being real in the same place is co-presence, not a link.

constraints.condition: spare connection capacity in community water and wastewater systems
constraints.activity: additional housing development in the eight counties
constraints.means: a plausible limiting condition exists; its effect is not established
evidence: EPA SDWIS: 210 active systems, 161,122 connections, 373,733 served
constraints.why: the systems are observed and their headroom is not. A small system is not a full one.

constraints.condition: the deed restriction caps rent at 80% of area median income
constraints.activity: recovery of any additional development or operating cost
constraints.means: a rule or limit demonstrably applies to this activity. It says what MAY NOT happen. It does not say that this is what currently limits output -- another condition may bind first.
unresolved_alternatives: water and wastewater service capacity (CM_WATER_SEWER_CAPACITY, capacity UNKNOWN)
evidence: S-06 deed-restriction purchase by the county
r38_feasibility: debt service exceeds the ceiling above a 4.646% coupon
constraints.why: R3.15 called this THE binding constraint. The attempt is kept here and now FAILS, which is the correction. The cap is verified -- it demonstrably applies, and the arithmetic against it is real -- but binding means it determines feasible OUTPUT, and that claim rules out the alternatives. Eight of housing production's eleven components are unobserved or proxied, so five candidates remain live and any of them could bind first. A project that cannot obtain water service is limited by water whatever the rent cap says.
constraints.refused: K_RENT_CEILING: BINDING_ECONOMIC_CONSTRAINT refused — it requires evidence that the condition determines feasible OUTPUT, not only that a rule applies. A limit on what may happen is a VERIFIED_RESTRICTION; ALSO naming this condition as THE one that binds rules out the others, and these remain unresolved and could bind first: water and wastewater service capacity (CM_WATER_SEWER_CAPACITY, capacity UNKNOWN), serviced land (CM_SERVICED_LAND, existence UNKNOWN), construction credit (CM_CONSTRUCTION_CREDIT, UNKNOWN), building trades capacity (CM_TRADES_LABOR, PROXY_ONLY), entitlement and permission (CM_ENTITLEMENT_PERMIT, PARTIALLY_OBSERVED).

constraints.condition: a construction or conduit coupon above about 4.3-4.6%
constraints.activity: covering debt service out of restricted rent
constraints.means: becomes limiting when stated assumptions hold; the scenario must be named
constraints.scenario: a 35-year fully debt-financed structure at the observed all-in cost
evidence: r38_feasibility break-even 4.646% low cost / 4.295% high cost
constraints.why: conditional on a coupon Dula does not hold. The scenario is named, which is what a conditional classification requires.

shared_headroom.what: the capital a project can absorb beyond its observed cost, and the monthly operating budget it can afford, ARE THE SAME MONEY
shared_headroom.correction_of_r314: R3.14 computed the capital form and showed it against water connection cost. That invites the reading that the whole of it is available for water. It is not.
shared_headroom.identity: capital headroom = (monthly headroom x 12) / annuity factor, exactly

competing_claims.claim: water and wastewater connection or extension
competing_claims.obtain: the utility's connection-fee schedule, or the water and sewer lines in a filed development budget
the operating pro forma in the bond Official Statement, or NM MFA owner-reported operating data
the reserve covenant in the bond indenture

competing_claims.claim: property tax or payment in lieu
competing_claims.obtain: the county ordinance and any PILOT agreement
the public housing authority's utility allowance schedule
the project's lease-up reporting to the county

shared_headroom.reading: At a 4.00% coupon the project has $44,988 per unit of room on the low cost estimate. That same room is $200.86 per unit per month of operating budget. A water connection at $44,988 a unit would consume ALL of it and leave nothing for management, maintenance, insurance, reserves or any payment in lieu of tax. Six claims compete for one pot and none of them is priced.

interventions.name: Verified service capacity, bought before it is needed
interventions.economic_problem: land cannot be developed into housing unless a water and wastewater system will serve it. Whether any system in the eight counties has headroom is not observed, so the cost of service is not a line a developer can put in a budget -- it is a risk they must price, and an unpriceable risk is priced as a refusal.

mechanism.initiating_condition: a capacity study and, where short, a plant or line upgrade
mechanism.affected_actor: community water system; the developer that would connect
mechanism.transmission: service capacity becomes a known quantity, and a connection becomes a priced line item rather than an open risk
mechanism.operating_or_financial_consequence: a known cost can be financed; an unknown one cannot be underwritten at any price
mechanism.potential_actor_response: a developer proceeds, or the system refuses service and the site is abandoned earlier and more cheaply

actors.actor: community water system or county utility
actors.must: authorise and operate the upgrade; state how many connections it will accept
hold the capacity-development reviews that would establish the baseline

actors.actor: NM Finance Authority / USDA Rural Development
actors.note: named as the conventional sources; no application, award or term for this region is held

capital.why: no connection fee, line-extension cost or plant-upgrade cost is held for any system in the region

recurring.why: operating cost of additional capacity is not held

study_cost.why: the capacity study is the cheapest item on this list and its cost is still not held

instruments: developer-funded extension recovered through connection fees
a county gap contribution of the kind already observed here
financing.note: the instruments are named because they are the conventional ones, not because any is observed to be available for this purpose here

direct_effects.what: the project's capital and operating headroom at a given coupon
direct_effects.unit: USD per unit / USD per unit-month
direct_effects.basis: r38_feasibility._annuity on an observed cost and a published rent limit; see shared_headroom

proposed_mechanisms.what: the connection cost becomes a known quantity

dependencies: a system exists that is willing to serve the site at all
the land is entitled for the use
the upgrade's cost is recoverable from someone
the resulting connection cost fits inside the headroom ALONGSIDE operating expenses, reserves and tax, which it must share

risks.risk: the capacity study finds ample headroom and the intervention is unnecessary
risks.note: this is a GOOD outcome and a total loss of the capital spent on the upgrade

risks.risk: water is available and something else binds -- land, labour, entitlement, credit
risks.note: eight of the eleven housing components are unobserved or proxied

risks.risk: the connection cost exceeds the shared headroom
risks.note: then the project needs more subordinate capital, which is R1

risks.risk: a system serving under 500 people cannot absorb the upgrade's operating cost

financial.what: project feasibility at a given coupon

regional.what: development capacity in the eight counties

household.basis: the deed restriction caps it; it does not move with any of this, which is why a water cost lands on feasibility and not on the tenant

validation.test: per-system permitted capacity, current demand and willingness to serve
validation.settles: whether K_SERVICE_CAPACITY is binding or irrelevant

validation.test: the water and sewer line items in a filed development budget

validation.settles: which row of the headroom table applies

household.pathway: rent is capped by the deed restriction, so a cheaper connection does not reach a tenant as a lower rent. It reaches them only if it is the difference between the units existing and not existing.
household.why_not_established: whether this project is marginal on water cost is unknown; it is financed and proceeding.

strength.claim: coherence: a known capacity is a precondition for any fit question about water and housing
capital mobilisation: a priceable risk can be financed

interventions.effects_note: effects with no evidence are held as PROPOSED MECHANISMS and are not reported as direct effects

demonstrations.question: What would make a regional food-distribution route economically viable?

constraints.means: a plausible limiting condition exists; its effect is not established
constraints.why: the second attempt that must fail. A cost existing does not establish that a business is unprofitable; that requires its revenue, and no order value, margin or stop count is held for any route.
constraints.refused: K_TRANSPORT_COST: BINDING_ECONOMIC_CONSTRAINT requires an OBSERVED LINK between 'a 262-mile northern loop costs $341-$676' and 'any northern food-distribution business'. Both being real in the same place is co-presence, not a link.

constraints.condition: small rural orders against a fixed loop cost
constraints.activity: hub and distributor service north of Santa Fe
constraints.means: evidence establishes that this condition limits this activity -- typically an actor observed acting on it
evidence: model/capacity.yaml: condition exists_uneconomic for distribution north of Santa Fe; hubs turn away distant buyers
constraints.why: the link IS observed here, and it is observed as BEHAVIOUR rather than as accounting: hubs that exist are recorded refusing distant buyers. That is an operator acting on the economics, which is stronger evidence of a limit than a cost figure, and weaker than a route's books.

constraints.condition: existing fleet mileage could carry local product
constraints.means: proposed as an explanation; requires investigation
evidence: The Food Depot: ~400,000 miles/yr, 9 counties, 150+ sites
constraints.why: if true the relevant cost is marginal rather than the cost of a dedicated loop, which changes every number on this page. It is untested.

operating_model.title: Route economics, simplified
operating_model.not_a_business_model: this is the driving, and only the driving. It has no vehicle depreciation, insurance, overhead, shrink, payment terms or seasonality. Every one of those makes the real requirement HIGHER, so what it computes is a FLOOR.
operating_model.identity_1: required contribution per stop = (route cost + other uncovered) / stops
operating_model.identity_2: required sales per stop = required contribution per stop / margin

observed.state: DOCUMENTED PER-MILE INPUTS, not a measured route cost

adjustable.name: delivery stops per loop
adjustable.why_default_1: ten was an invented operating assumption and is removed. One stop bearing the whole loop is the worst case and a true upper bound, so the default view still shows the most a stop could be asked to carry rather than a guess at how many stops a route has.

adjustable.name: route operating cost
adjustable.obtain: already held: $341-$676 on documented per-mile inputs

adjustable.name: other uncovered route costs
adjustable.obtain: the operator's own cost accounting; defaults to zero so the result stays a floor

adjustable.name: contribution margin
adjustable.definition: contribution margin = (sales − variable cost of goods and handling) / sales. NOT gross margin and NOT net margin.
adjustable.obtain: a distributor's income statement; at zero no sales figure is shown

operating_model.defaults_note: every unknown defaults to zero or to the observed low end. No operating assumption is inserted, so the default view shows the least the route must recover, not a guess at what it does.

interventions.name: Carry local product on existing fleet mileage
interventions.economic_problem: a dedicated northern loop must recover $341-$676 from its stops. An existing route passing the same stops has already recovered it, so the relevant cost is incremental handling and time.

mechanism.initiating_condition: an operator with existing northern mileage agrees to carry third-party local product
mechanism.affected_actor: The Food Depot or a comparable fleet; northern producers; institutional buyers
mechanism.transmission: fixed route cost is already sunk against the existing purpose, so local product faces marginal cost rather than average cost
mechanism.changed_variable: cost per stop attributable to local product
mechanism.operating_or_financial_consequence: the contribution a stop must make falls to the incremental cost, which is unobserved but is bounded above by the dedicated-loop figure
mechanism.potential_actor_response: a hub that currently refuses a distant buyer accepts one

actors.must: have spare capacity, permission and willingness to carry third-party product
actors.note: the mileage is observed; the capacity and the willingness are not
97 institutional buyers in the entity population

capital.why: may be none, or may be refrigeration and handling equipment on an existing vehicle

recurring.why: incremental handling, time and liability per stop are not held

instruments: an operating agreement rather than capital
repayment_source: a fee per stop or per case
financing.note: this intervention may need little or no capital, which is precisely why it is worth testing before the ones that do

direct_effects.what: cost per stop on a dedicated loop
cost per stop on an existing route

dependencies: the existing route passes near the producers and the buyers
the operator has legal and practical capacity to carry third-party product
cold chain is maintained for products that need it

risks.risk: the fleet has no spare capacity
carrying third-party product conflicts with the operator's charitable purpose or insurance
schedules do not match institutional delivery windows

validation.test: whether existing northern mileage has spare capacity and permission to carry local product
validation.settles: K_BACKHAUL, and with it whether any capital is needed at all

validation.test: incremental cost per stop of adding local product to an existing run

household.pathway: a higher realised price for a producer is household income for a farm household
household.why_not_established: no producer's realised price is held, before or after any change

strength.claim: complexity: more buyer-producer relationships actually trading
coherence: an existing asset and an unmet need are made to fit

interventions.effects_note: effects with no evidence are held as PROPOSED MECHANISMS and are not reported as direct effects

interventions.name: Coordinated procurement to raise order density
interventions.economic_problem: the loop cost is fixed and the orders are small. Raising the value per stop raises the contribution without changing the driving.

mechanism.initiating_condition: buyers in one valley place a combined order
mechanism.transmission: fewer, larger stops against the same route cost
mechanism.changed_variable: required contribution per stop, and order value per stop
mechanism.operating_or_financial_consequence: the route covers its cost at a lower total sales volume
mechanism.potential_actor_response: a hub that refused a valley now serves it

actors.note: no such body is observed for northern food procurement

recurring.why: the coordinator's time is a real recurring cost and is not held

instruments: programme funding of a coordinator role
repayment_source: none: this is a cost, not an investment
financing.note: CM_PROGRAM_FUNDING is the one component in the region with an OBSERVED capacity, which makes it the most concrete source on this page

direct_effects.what: required contribution per stop falls as stops consolidate
direct_effects.basis: route_economics: the same route cost over fewer, larger stops

dependencies: buyers are close enough to share a stop
procurement rules permit a combined award

risks.risk: institutional procurement rules fragment awards by design
risks.note: constraint C09 records exactly this: demand fragmented into small awards and filtered through kitchens

risks.risk: coordination lapses when the funding does
risks.note: constraint C03: local wholesale demand depends on time-limited public purchasing programmes

financial.basis: route_economics, conditional on stops and margin

validation.test: stops per loop and order value per stop
validation.settles: whether consolidation closes the gap or only narrows it

validation.test: whether procurement rules permit combined awards
validation.settles: whether this intervention is legal before it is economic

household.why_not_established: an institutional buyer's spend reaching a producer household depends on the producer's margin, which is not held

strength.claim: us-ness: coordinated procurement is collective action, and would be observable as such

interventions.effects_note: effects with no evidence are held as PROPOSED MECHANISMS and are not reported as direct effects

comparison.no_score: no intervention score, expected return, impact multiplier or ranking is computed. With no recurring cost, no capacity effect and no operating economics on either side, any ranking would be ordering the interventions by how confidently they were written.

what_would_make_this_decision_ready: a capital cost for the water upgrade, from any system in the region
an incremental cost per stop for carrying local product on an existing route
a contribution margin for any northern distributor
a capacity figure for any shared component, which would allow a shared CONSTRAINT to be asserted instead of a shared exposure

classes.SHARED_EXPOSURE: two activities depend on the same resource or economic condition
classes.SHARED_CONSTRAINT: the same bottleneck limits both. Requires the shared object to be a demonstrated constraint, which requires a known capacity
classes.POTENTIAL_COMPLEMENTARITY: improving one could benefit the other; the mechanism is stated and unmeasured
classes.DEMONSTRATED_COMPLEMENTARITY: evidence establishes a measurable relationship between them
classes.PORTFOLIO_EFFECT: a supported change in financial performance, risk or productive outcome across the investments

portfolio.geography_is_not_a_relation: two investments in the same county share a map, not an economic relationship. Shared geography cannot be passed to the classifier.

relations.b: R5 Santa Fe Midtown horizontal infrastructure
relations.means: two activities depend on the same resource or economic condition
relations.why: both are development that must be served by a community water system. Whether that system limits either is unknown, so this is exposure.
relations.refused: R1 workforce housing/R5 Santa Fe Midtown horizontal infrastructure: SHARED_CONSTRAINT requires a known capacity on CM_WATER_SEWER_CAPACITY. Without one, two activities needing the same thing is a SHARED EXPOSURE and not a shared limit -- the thing may be abundant.

relations.means: two activities depend on the same resource or economic condition
relations.why: housing needs service water and food production needs delivered water; both draw on a basin whose delivery is unobserved. Real exposure, unknown magnitude.

relations.means: improving one could benefit the other; the mechanism is stated and unmeasured
relations.why: a route that becomes viable for food could carry other regional goods. The mechanism is stated and nothing measures it.

relations.b: R7 interim accommodation for the laboratory
relations.means: two activities depend on the same resource or economic condition
relations.why: the attempt that must fail. Both need building trades, and that two projects draw on one labour pool is as likely to be competition as complementarity.
relations.refused: R1 workforce housing/R7 interim accommodation for the laboratory: DEMONSTRATED_COMPLEMENTARITY requires an observed measurable relationship

portfolio.why_none_demonstrated: every shared object in the representation has capacity UNKNOWN. A demonstrated complementarity needs a measured relationship, and a measured relationship through a shared object needs that object's capacity.

household.buffer_identity: recurring disposable resources − necessary recurring costs
household.rule: greater production and investor return do not imply better household outcomes. R3.6 observed the counter-case directly: Los Alamos real median income did not move while production doubled.

pathways.why: the deed restriction caps the rent. A cheaper connection does not reach the tenant as a lower rent; it reaches them only as the difference between the units existing and not existing.
a servable site is a home with water. Whether any household is currently without because of service capacity is not observed.
a producer's realised price is household income for a farm household. No producer's realised price is held, before or after.
steadier institutional demand could steady farm employment. C03 records that this demand depends on time-limited public programmes, which argues the other way.

household.buffer_status: neither term of the identity is held at household level. ACS medians are DIFFERENT HOUSEHOLDS -- the median-income household is not the median-rent household -- so differencing them produces no household's buffer.
